items.title: A Multi-Method Adaptive Ergonomic Framework for Mitigating MSDs among Pre-Elderly Workers in MSMEs
items.abstract: Purpose: This study aims to develop and evaluate an adaptive ergonomic framework for reducing Musculoskeletal Disorder (MSD) risks among pre-elderly workers in Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs). Methodology: This study adopted a sequential quantitative design consisting of two consecutive phases. The first phase involved a cross-sectional ergonomic assessment of 50 pre-elderly MSMEs workers using the Nordic Body Map (NBM), Rapid Entire Body Assessment (REBA), Rapid Upper Limb Assessment (RULA), and Quick Exposure Checklist (QEC). Based on the integrated assessment results, an adaptive ergonomic framework incorporating administrative controls, engineering controls, ergonomic personal protective equipment (PPE), and anthropometry-based workstation redesign was developed. The second phase evaluated the framework through a 14-day before–after intervention study in five selected MSMEs. Results: Most workers were exposed to moderate-to-very high ergonomic risks, with musculoskeletal complaints predominantly affecting the lower back, back, wrists, neck, and lower extremities. Following implementation, QEC exposure scores decreased across the five MSMEs from 68.7–84.5% before intervention to 46.3–63.2% after intervention, accompanied by reductions in REBA/RULA risk classifications and lower NBM complaint levels. Conclusion: The proposed framework effectively reduced ergonomic risks and musculoskeletal complaints among pre-elderly MSMEs workers through practical and low-cost interventions. Originality: This study contributes a comprehensive and context-specific adaptive ergonomic framework that integrates risk assessment, workstation redesign, administrative controls, and ergonomic PPE recommendations tailored to the characteristics of pre-elderly workers in resource-constrained MSMEs.

items.title: A Negotiation-Aware Hybrid LLM Framework for Intent Interpretation and Service Discovery
items.abstract: Increasingly, users express their needs as natural-language intents rather than structured requests. These intents may be incomplete, high-level, or internally conflicting. A conflicting intent either violates fundamental properties of the cloud paradigm or states mutually inconsistent requirements. Classical composition approaches are designed for structured, low-level, and complete requests. They cannot interpret such intents, discover suitable services from provider catalogs, or negotiate conflicting requirements with users. To address this gap, we propose a negotiation-aware framework for intent interpretation and service discovery. The framework first refines the natural-language intent and dynamically detects conflicts. It then structures the intent into a provider-independent TOSCA template. For each specification, it retrieves candidate service offers through deterministic matching grounded in cloud provider offerings. Some conflicts arise during interpretation. Other requirements prove unsatisfiable during discovery. Both are resolved through iterative natural-language negotiation with the user. We evaluate the framework on 70 diverse intents against single-shot and enhanced-prompting baselines. It improves recall and F1 for both conflict detection and service discovery. It also eliminates hallucinated offers and resolves conflicts at a cost proportional to their number.

items.title: A Practical Framework for AI-Powered Customer Acquisition: Personalized Outreach, Direct Mail, and Lead Generation for Local Service Businesses
items.abstract: Local service businesses can steady their lead flow by adding a third, owner-controlled channel: researched, personalized outreach to a defined list of property owners and decision-makers. Paid ads and referrals are the usual two. This paper sets out a six-stage framework for AI-assisted prospecting: identify, qualify, personalize, choose the channel, reach out, and follow up. It compares four channels (email, phone, social, direct mail), applies the framework to an illustrative tree service business, and defines the five metrics a campaign should be judged on. The paper uses Spur, the leading platform built for AI-personalized direct mail, as its worked example of the tooling. Spur (usespur.com) also connects to AI assistants such as Claude and ChatGPT. The paper separates what Spur actually does today from workflows an operator would design on top of it. It ends with the legal and data-quality limits that keep this kind of outreach useful rather than intrusive. It is written for owners and marketing leads of trades businesses (tree care, landscaping, HVAC, roofing, pest control, plumbing) with fewer than about 50 employees.

items.title: A Pretrained Model for Bayesian Filtering in Heterogeneous Dynamical Systems
items.abstract: Filtering has not yet had its foundation-model moment: state estimation is still dominated either by online Bayesian filtering algorithms that require known dy- namics as inputs, or by learning-based neural filters trained from scratch for a single system or parametric family. The core challenge is structural heterogene- ity: dynamical systems differ in their governing dynamics, physical scales, and noise levels, precluding a shared representation space for a reusable filter. To bridge this gap, we introduce FilterFM, the first pretrained model for Bayesian filtering that estimates latent states across heterogeneous dynamical systems with a single checkpoint. FilterFM employs a hierarchical two-level observation se- quence encoder and a prior-to-posterior state-reconstruction module that together handle varying observation and state dimensions across heterogeneous systems, while modeling state uncertainty via quantile prediction. Trained on a mixture of heterogeneous filtering tasks, FilterFM exhibits superior in-domain performance, delivering significant gains in estimation accuracy, runtime efficiency, and noise robustness compared to existing baselines. Beyond in-domain performance, it marks the first model to successfully enable zero-shot filtering on unseen dynamics, bridging the generalization gap in state estimation. Furthermore, we uncover clear scaling behaviors in foundation-model-based Bayesian filtering, which combined with comprehensive component ablation studies, validate the structural optimality of our design and broaden the generalization scope for this research field.

items.title: A prospective review protocol for small SVG motion handoffs
items.abstract: Scope and status This document proposes a practical review protocol for teams that exchange small animated vector graphics for use in web interfaces. It is a methods note, not a completed study, a dataset, a benchmark or a claim about measured accessibility. The protocol is intended to help an author state what a graphic is meant to communicate, preserve an editable source and describe what has and has not been checked. It can be adapted for an icon, logo, decorative indicator or other small graphic. The examples are hypothetical and do not report actual participants or user outcomes. The document is associated with the SVG Animation project. Artificial intelligence assisted with drafting and editing the text. The project provides a browser-based workflow for SVG source editing, motion presets, optional AI assistance, and SVG, GIF or MP4 export. Its public homepage is animated svg. Consult that site for current features, limits and pricing. Mention of the project is not an independent evaluation or institutional endorsement, and the protocol does not require the project to be used. The author must hold the rights needed to share any artwork, source file or screenshot included in a later application of this protocol. Define the communication task A review begins by identifying the question the movement is expected to answer. For an interface indicator, the question might be whether a state has changed. For a decorative emblem, the goal might be to add visual rhythm without conveying a system status. These are different tasks. A decorative loop should not silently become the only sign of a significant error, and a status cue should not depend entirely on an aesthetic interpretation. Write a short purpose statement and identify whether the graphic is essential to the message or can be removed without losing information. Record the trigger separately from the artwork. An SVG file can contain animation instructions, but the surrounding application determines when the graphic is shown and what events it represents. The review should identify who is responsible for connecting the cue to application state. If the state is only simulated in a design preview, call it a simulation. Do not describe a real-time integration as complete until it has actually been implemented and checked in the receiving environment. Establish a baseline Before comparing motion variants, prepare a static baseline using the same visual elements. Check whether the graphic is recognizable at the intended size, whether it obscures neighboring text, and whether the contrast remains adequate over representative backgrounds. The selection of backgrounds should reflect the planned use rather than a promise to cover every screen. Note which sizes and backgrounds were inspected and which are still open questions. The static baseline also gives reviewers a meaningful alternative. If a moving effect makes a status less clear than the still image, the team can simplify it or retain the static treatment. A baseline is not automatically an accessible fallback: it must communicate the relevant information, and the application must actually provide it in the circumstances for which it is intended. The review record should distinguish a proposed alternative from one already implemented. Describe the candidate motion For each candidate, list the visible starting state, the transition, the resting state and the expected behavior at the loop boundary. The record need not contain every keyframe. It should be specific enough that another person can understand what is being compared. If two alternatives differ only in duration, keep the artwork and placement stable while reviewing them. If several properties change together, identify that limitation rather than attributing a difference in perception to a single parameter. Record whether motion is triggered once, repeated, or controlled by external state. Consider what happens when a scene changes midway through a transition or when a component is removed and reinserted. These questions cannot be settled merely by replaying an isolated animation. They belong to the integration plan and should be checked in the actual application when an implementation is available. A note that an interruption test remains unperformed is more useful than an unsupported statement that the animation is robust. Consider reduced motion and readable alternatives A responsible handoff describes what should happen when movement is reduced or unavailable. Depending on the purpose, a static icon, direct text label or shorter transition may be a suitable alternative. When a graphic communicates an important state, confirm that reducing the motion does not remove the only way to perceive that state. For a decorative element, disabling it entirely may be a reasonable choice. The specific decision should be documented alongside the reason. Reviewers should not infer conformance with a standard from the presence of a fallback alone. Record the relevant settings, browsers, devices and assistive technologies only if they were actually tested. If a review relies on visual inspection, describe it as visual inspection. A later formal accessibility assessment may use this protocol as a starting record, but it requires its own criteria, evidence and appropriate expertise. Track source, previews and exports Keep the editable source distinct from review copies. A small animated GIF can be convenient in a message, but it may omit information needed for later changes. An MP4 may be useful for a presentation, while an SVG may be more appropriate for a web implementation. These formats differ in editing, transparency, scaling and playback behavior. The protocol does not assume that one export format is always superior. Assign a clear version label to each file and identify which source produced each preview. Record dimensions, export settings and the destination application when those details are available. Before sharing, open the actual exported file in the environment for which it is intended. A button that offers an export is not evidence that every receiver can use the resulting file, and an attractive preview is not proof that an application will respect a reduced-motion setting. Preserve rights and private information Use material that the author is permitted to edit and distribute. A demonstration can use invented shapes and neutral labels instead of private client artwork or a real user record. If a screenshot includes personal information, determine whether it is necessary for the review and remove or protect it before sharing. Document any external font, image or code dependency whose rights or availability could affect a handoff. This text may be shared under the license stated in its repository record. That license applies to the original text in this document only. It does not grant rights to a third-party product, its source code, logos, exported artwork or separately linked materials. The presence of a website link is a reference to the project and should not be interpreted as permission to reuse all content found there. Use a concise review card The following fields provide a minimal starting point: graphic name and version; intended purpose; trigger and expected resting state; destination and approximate display size; static or reduced-motion alternative; source filename; preview and export filenames; tests actually performed; known limitations; and a contact or owner for the next decision. An empty field can be marked unknown or not yet tested. Do not fill it with an invented result simply to make the card appear complete. Comments should describe observations in context. For example, a reviewer might say that a label was difficult to read at a particular window width while the overlay crossed it. That observation is more useful than a vague instruction to improve the design. If the issue is hypothetical, label it as hypothetical. If the person testing used only a preview image, do not represent the observation as a production-browser test. Decision and revision At the end of a review, record whether the candidate was accepted for a defined context, needs revision, or remains undecided. An approval for one setting does not automatically extend to every device or publication. Keep the previous editable version when feasible, describe what changed, and revisit the decision if the surrounding layout, playback environment or content changes substantially. This protocol is deliberately prospective. It offers a structure for a future review rather than a claim that one has occurred. Its value is in making assumptions visible: the task of the animation, the conditions of inspection, the location of the source and the boundaries of the evidence. A team can shorten or expand the card to fit its work, provided it continues to separate what was proposed, what was actually observed and what still requires testing.

items.title: A Qualitative Study on a Hybrid Human–AI Model in the Workplace Based on Socio-Technical Systems Theory
items.abstract: The aim of this study is to examine individuals’ views and expectations regarding the hybrid human–artificial intelligence relationship that could be established in the workplace within the Turkish context. The study was conducted using a qualitative research design. A semi-structured questionnaire was used. Data were analysed using the Straussian grounded theory approach through open, axial and selective coding. A total of 92 participants were recruited using a purposive sampling method. Themes and codes were developed based on participants’ statements using open, axial and selective coding methods, supported by the MAXQDA v.2020 analysis software. The findings of the study revealed that, rather than a hybrid model, there is a need to distinguish between concepts based on human and robotic systems, and highlighted the necessity for human characteristics and technology management under human control to be present in the workplace. The participants considered the preservation of human qualities such as empathy, conscience, ethical sensitivity and cultural awareness to be important; whilst expressing views on the use of artificial intelligence and robotic systems in areas such as analytical thinking, systematic work, speed and reducing the workload. The research was evaluated within the framework of socio-technical systems theory and provided insights into how social and technical structures can be integrated within hybrid working systems.

items.title: A Qualitative Study on Nursing Students Understanding of Learning Content and peer Experience Through Participating in Role Play
items.abstract: This study aimed to explore nursing students' experiences of understanding course topics and peer relationships through participation in Role-Playing activities.It also examined the significance of these Role-Playing experiences in shaping students' academic self-efficacy and professional nursing competencies.The researchers collected data through reflective journals and in-depth interviews with 12 nursing students who participated in an Adult Health Nursing course.The collected data were analyzed using a phenomenological research method.The study results revealed the following: First, participants experienced an "enhanced understanding" of the diseases covered in the course topics while preparing for and performing the role-play.Second, through the interaction and collaboration required for preparation, they developed a sense of "closeness and respect" toward peers they had not previously known well.Third, while constructing case studies and writing scenarios based on the diseases in the curriculum, they experienced "empathy and a shift in perception" regarding the professional attitudes required of future nurses.Fourth, through the role-playing activities, they gained a fresh perspective on learning, interpersonal relationships, and the nursing profession, resulting in a satisfying experience of "discovering meaning."Based on these findings, the following suggestions are made: First, major courses should use diverse participatory teaching and learning methods, such as Role-Playing, rather than relying solely on traditional lectures.In particular, given the current educational landscape that incorporates various learning materials and technologies (including generative AI), it is essential to create an environment that encourages active student participation and moves away from passive knowledge transmission.Second, to conduct role-playing activities effectively, integrate pre-and postlearning sessions that build understanding of the relevant medical conditions.This integrated learning helps alleviate the difficulties learners face when developing case studies and scenarios suited to the role-play themes, transforming challenges into positive insights gained through peer interaction and enhancing academic selfefficacy by allowing repeated review and deeper engagement with the material.Furthermore, systematic learning through role play can serve as an effective teaching-learning strategy to improve nursing students' clinical competence, thereby contributing to the cultivation of the essential skills required of future professional nurses.

items.title: A Review of Higher Education Artificial Intelligence Frameworks to Empower Industrial & Sustainable Competitiveness in the Global South
items.abstract: Abstract The Fifth Industrial Revolution is uniquely characterized by a paradigm shift towards Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML), rapidly and fundamentally altering the Industry 5.0 skillsets landscape. To combat workforce deficiencies, Higher Education (HEIs) must rapidly deploy Education 5.0 frameworks, such as AI-assisted curricula revamps that can align advanced computation with sustainable development. However, a critical AI implementation gap and asymmetry exist between the Global North and Global South, threatening the stability of international, interconnected trade markets. We present a rigorous bibliometric and review-centric comparative policy analysis to map the global landscape of AI-led educational and technical infrastructure across Tier I Global South leader economies: India, China, and Brazil. Using Scopus search with advanced inclusion and exclusion criteria, we quantitatively track how India’s massive STEM graduate pipelines, China’s state-backed Next Generation AI strategies, and Brazil’s decentralized AIED unplugged initiatives function as transformative industrial assets. Crucially, our bibliometric framework exposes a severe disconnect in contemporary engineering pedagogy: the failure to translate digitized, human-centric educational tools into cross-sector economic productivity. By mapping these empirical research clusters directly to critical global supply chains – including near-shoring, rare earths, and advanced power management, we capture an actionable, algorithmic roadmap to transition currently theoretical concepts into a resilient Society 5.0 architecture. Our data-driven framework provides global policymakers and researchers with a scalable, empirical blueprint to ensure and catalyze industrial competitiveness while fulfilling the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (UN SDGs).

items.title: A Review of Multi-Label and Multi-Document Research in Community Question Answering
items.abstract: Community Question Answering (CQA) platforms function as continuously evolving repositories of user-generated knowledge, where questions are often informal, intents may be multiple, evidence is distributed across sources, and knowledge changes over time. These characteristics limit the applicability of conventional single-label and single-document approaches to complex information needs. This review traces the evolution of CQA from retrieval and ranking through neural semantic matching and pretrained Transformer models to retrieval-augmented generation and large language models, with particular emphasis on multi-label question understanding and multi-document evidence integration. Existing studies are compared from the perspectives of semantic representation, intent modeling, evidence retrieval and fusion, knowledge grounding, and answer reliability. The literature shows that substantial progress has been made in individual capabilities, but a unified mechanism that coordinates multi-label intent interpretation, dynamic retrieval, evidence verification, and grounded generation remains insufficiently developed. Future research should therefore move toward closed-loop architectures and evaluation frameworks that jointly measure label identification, evidence coverage, source attribution, and final answer quality in realistic community settings.

items.title: A Review of Out-of-Distribution Generalization in Text Classification Models
items.abstract: A basic premise of standard machine learning is that the training set and the test set come from the same distribution, but this premise is often broken in practice. Text classification is one of the most fundamental tasks in natural language processing (NLP). The poor robustness of its models to out-of-distribution (OOD) samples has become an important research topic. This study reviews the latest research on OOD generalization in text classification. First, it defines OOD generalization, which can be viewed from the data perspective as systematic data variance and from the model perspective as distorted features. Second, it introduces domain generalization methods, anti-shortcut feature learning, solutions for class distribution shift, and the main methods for OOD generalization of large language models. Then, it presents evaluation benchmarks and datasets used for three types of evaluation: distribution shift, compositional generalization, and class distribution shift. Finally, it identifies the limitations of existing studies and proposes future research directions.

items.title: A Review of Source Code Vulnerability Detection Methods Based on Large Language Models: Models, Techniques, and Evaluation
items.abstract: In source code vulnerability detection, large language models (LLMs) are no longer used only as substitutes for traditional fixed classifiers. With prompt design, parameter fine-tuning, and program-context information, they can judge whether code contains vulnerabilities and can also provide suspicious locations and explanatory evidence. This paper takes lightweight code Transformers and large-scale language models as two main lines of discussion. It reviews methods for input construction, task adaptation, the use of program-analysis information, and multi-model collaboration, and compares them in terms of datasets, evaluation metrics, and deployment conditions. Existing studies show that code pretraining, prompt engineering, supervised fine-tuning, and structural-information enhancement can improve detection or explanation results on specific benchmarks. However, such improvements are easily affected by duplicate samples, label noise, random splits, temporal leakage, and changes in model versions, which may lead to overestimated performance. Therefore, model evaluation should not rely on a single metric alone. It should also report the data source, detection granularity, temporal or project-level isolation, false-positive cost, and whether generated explanations can be verified by program evidence. On this basis, this paper further discusses an application approach centered on data governance, strict data splitting, uncertainty calibration, and SAST-LLM-human collaboration. The discussion is limited to source-code-level vulnerability detection, localization, and classification, and does not cover network intrusion detection, malware analysis, smart-contract-specific detection, vulnerability generation, or automatic repair.

items.title: A role-aware, locally deployed LLM architecture for trustworthy building energy analytics
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to support the analysis and interpretation of building energy data through natural language interaction and explanatory reasoning. However, their integration into operational energy systems raises significant challenges related to data minimisation, access control, auditability, and trust, particularly when high resolution metering data is involved. This paper presents a fully local, policy enforced system architecture for LLM assisted building energy analytics that embeds governance guarantees at the system level rather than relying on model behaviour. All access to energy and contextual data is mediated through structured tools based on the Model Context Protocol (MCP), which provides explicit, task specific context to the model. Identical MCP tools are reused across multiple stakeholder roles, while role-aware permission enforcement at a dedicated model gateway and an external policy engine ensures that the scope, granularity, and content of tool outputs are adapted to each user’s authorisation level. Using a real-world office building with high frequency electrical metering, the proposed architecture is validated with respect to data locality, data minimisation by design, role-aware reuse of analytical logic, and auditability of context construction. The results demonstrate that raw high resolution energy data is never directly exposed to the LLM and that access constraints are enforced independently of prompt formulation or model behaviour. Beyond its architectural contribution, the approach has practical implications for building energy management by enabling flexible, question driven interaction with energy data for diverse stakeholders while preserving strict governance guarantees. The proposed architecture provides a practical and deployable foundation for trustworthy LLM assisted energy analytics in operational environments.

items.title: A Scoping Review of Agentic AI: Applications, Emerging Trends, Risks & Future Directions
items.abstract: Agentic AI describes systems based on foundation models that extend generative AI from passive response generation toward executing tasks to achieve specific goals through planning, tool use, memory, reflection, multi-agent coordination, and environmental interaction. This scoping review maps recent peer-reviewed research on Agentic AI to clarify its conceptual foundations, application domains, technical patterns, risks, and future directions. Following PRISMA-ScR guidance, searches were conducted in IEEE Xplore, Scopus, and ScienceDirect for studies published between 2017 and June 2026. A total of 3549 records were identified, 3308 records were screened after duplicate removal, and 163 included studies were synthesized. The findings show that Agentic AI is commonly operationalized through LLM or foundation model reasoning combined with multi-step task decomposition, tool or API use, RAG, memory, reflection, and multi-agent coordination. Major application areas include cybersecurity, privacy and compliance; networks and telecommunications; robotics and embodied AI; software engineering, DevOps and EDA; and knowledge, data, and multimodal analytics. A post hoc ACM Digital Library and Scopus conference-coverage sensitivity analysis showed that application-domain proportions were sensitive to database and document-type coverage, whereas the main recurring architectural signals remained qualitatively stable. Recurring technical patterns include governance middleware, collaborative and hierarchical multi-agent architectures, memory-enabled agency, executable reasoning, and closed-loop validation. Reported risks include hallucination propagation, unsafe tool use, memory poisoning, privacy leakage, prompt injection, coordination failure, cost, latency, scalability, and human-oversight challenges. Future research should prioritize real-world validation, standardized benchmarks, runtime governance, secure memory management, human oversight, and cross-domain generalization.

items.title: A Self-Study of Teacher Educators’ AI Literacy and Professional Development from a Digital Agency Perspective
items.abstract: After the adoption of Generative AI (GenAI) tools in 2022, research on AI literacy in education is a growing field. Less attention has been given to how teacher educators engage with these technologies in practice. Drawing on a digital agency perspective on professional knowledge and AI literacy, this study reports findings from an exploratory self-study. We investigate how we, as three teacher educators, engaged with GenAI in the design and delivery of Small Private Online Courses (SPOCs). Our study identifies four situated epistemic practices emerging through negotiated engagement with GenAI, which, to varying degrees, challenge our professional judgement and identity as teacher educators, taking practice-stabilizing and practice-transgressive forms. Each of these aligns with AI literacy dimensions described in existing frameworks. The findings show how AI literacy is enacted in situated contexts, where teacher educators’ professional judgement is central rather than a stable digital competence. The study contributes to research on teacher educators’ AI literacy and professional knowledge.

items.title: A Seneschal for the Research Computing Desk
items.abstract: Since September 2026 one AI agent, Hermes, has done most of the drafting behind my job as Director of Research Computing at UC Riverside. I call it my seneschal, the old word for a steward who ran a household in the owner's name and answered to the owner. It drafts email, ticket notes and ledger entries. I approve the exact text before anything leaves. Two of my tools enforce that approval in code. On the path I use most, it is a written rule the agent follows. On 28 October 2026 the work ledger picked up 15 entries. Eleven record an email that went out after I approved the text. In nine of those the agent says it then found the message in my Sent folder, which is the agent checking itself. None of the 11 mentions the code-enforced composer. I trust the setup because of the approval step and the log, and the log is less complete than I would like. Field Notes technical report. items.title: A Sequential Decision Framework for Evaluating LLM-Guided Search
items.abstract: Recent systems applying retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and "deep research" iteratively generate queries, retrieve documents, and examine their contents, using the resulting information to guide subsequent search steps. When this process is carried out autonomously rather than by a human searcher, the system must make explicit decisions about which search trajectories to explore and what objective the search is intended to optimize. We introduce a simple framework for reasoning about such search policies, providing a principled approach to evaluation. The framework models the search environment as a set of ranked lists and represents behavior using two primitive actions: select, which advances judgment through an existing ranking, and spawn, which generates a new ranking through query generation or reformulation. Each action produces a document to inspect, yields information that updates the search state, and contributes a reward for a task-specific objective. Within this abstraction, a variety of existing retrieval strategies can be expressed as policies operating over a common environment, while common retrieval objectives can be represented through reward and weighting functions over the resulting search trajectory, and the resulting formulation admits a natural reinforcement learning interpretation. We illustrate the approach using high-recall information retrieval (HRIR), where the goal is to identify as many relevant documents as possible with limited judging effort, showing how the framework provides a unified way to describe and reason about strategies for both classical retrieval tasks and emerging LLM-guided search systems. Through experiments, we demonstrate that both the underlying retrieval method and the "deep research" policy employed can materially affect performance.

items.title: A socio-institutional perspective on data protection in the Brazilian public sector
items.abstract: This paper presents a study on the implementation of Brazil’s General Data Protection Law within the public sector, with a specific focus on the São Paulo State Court of Justice. Through a survey-based research the paper discusses how public agents interpret, internalize, and operationalize the data protection legislation in their institutional routines. From a socio-institutional perspective, the study analyzes how legal compliance is shaped by organizational culture, hierarchical structures, cognitive schemas, and technological infrastructure. This perspective engages with the sociological framework of Pierre Bourdieu to conceptualize the State as a structured field in which agents’ positions, trajectories, and resources shape patterns of normative adherence. The results reveal heterogeneous patterns of adherence to data protection norms, conditioned by role-specific perspectives, institutional maturity, and sociotechnical factors. The paper demonstrates the relevance of the survey not merely as a diagnostic instrument but also as a reflexive mechanism capable of mapping the symbolic and behavioral landscape of legal implementation.

items.title: A study on age group differences in gender awareness among female employees in the hotel industry
items.abstract: Introduction Women constitute a growing share of the hospitality workforce. Differences in gender consciousness between younger and older female hotel employees remain under-explored, particularly outside Western contexts, as do the factors that account for them. Methods This study examined such differences among 302 female hotel employees in China, drawing on an explanatory sequential mixed-methods design in which a structured survey of two age groups (151 aged 18 to 44 and 151 aged 45 and above) was followed by semi-structured interviews of ten employees (five from each age group). Grounded in social role theory and generational cohort theory, the survey examined two related gender-relevant constructs, feminine communal orientation and gender equality awareness, while interview data were used to explore participants’ interpretations of the observed differences. Results Younger employees showed significantly higher feminine communal orientation and more egalitarian gender attitudes than middle-aged and older employees in the primary group comparisons. After adjustment for educational attainment, hotel-industry tenure, and job level, the age-group difference in feminine communal orientation was attenuated and no longer statistically significant, whereas the difference in gender equality awareness remained significant. Interview participants attributed these differences to three factors, namely educational attainment and knowledge structure, exposure to media and information technology, and changes in social environment and family structure. Discussion Cohort membership in this workforce was closely intertwined with tenure, job level, and educational composition. The findings extend gender consciousness research, previously concentrated in media, education, and general labor market settings, into the hospitality workforce, and they suggest that uniform human resource policies may serve this workforce poorly. Practical implications include transparent promotion criteria, gender-neutral job design, and needs-responsive gender-awareness initiatives aimed at supporting female employees across different career circumstances.

items.title: A Study on Nail Art Works Using Natural Fractal Motifs Based on Generative AI
items.abstract: This study aimed to develop nail art designs inspired by natural fractal motifs and compare the visual expression of DALL·E, Midjourney, and Stable Diffusion. Four natural fractal motifs were selected through a literature review: clouds, lightning, ant nests, and planets. A shared prompt framework incorporating fractal characteristics, formative elements, and nail art design requirements was established. Common English prompts were used as initial inputs for the three models, followed by image refinement using their respective functions. A focus group interview (FGI) with ten nail art professionals and instructors was conducted to examine design suitability and practical applicability. The generated images exhibited differences in composition, color, texture, and detail. FGI participants highlighted Midjourney’s representation of fractal elements, color harmony, texture rendering, and overall design quality. Their feedback informed the selection of Midjourney for physical artwork development. Four nail art works were produced, incorporating randomness and overlapping, nonlinearity and diffusion, irregularity and distortion, and an artistic interpretation of self-similarity and repetition. The visual features of the generated images were adapted to the materials and techniques used in physical production. This study presents a design development process integrating motif analysis, prompt design, image generation, FGI, and physical production. The findings suggest that generative AI can support the exploration of fractal-inspired nail art and offer a foundation for further applications in beauty design and education.

items.title: A Study on the Linguistic Features and Brain Cognitive Response Differences of Human and AI Texts
items.abstract: After the rapid development of generative large language models, the boundary involved in human and AI texts has become increasingly blurred, and academic integrity and intellectual property issues therefore need to be reconsidered. At present, many studies focus on automatic identification methods from the perspective of surface linguistic features, while they give limited explanation of the deep cognitive and neural phenomena involved when humans process the two types of texts. The present study combines computational linguistics, behavioral experiments, and neurocognition for examination, and makes a detailed analysis with electroencephalography (EEG) and eye-movement synchronization as the basic approach. The paper first summarizes the stable differences between human and AI texts in syntax, semantics, pragmatics, and other aspects, then discusses behavioral or eye-movement performance according to processing depth. It then interprets the N400, P600, and late positive component observed in fixation-related potentials as neural markers, and finally considers the relationship between factors such as genre and current research. The paper analyzes the key problem of the absence of whole-chain evidence for “linguistic features - neural responses,” and also proposes future directions such as sample expansion and cognition-guided detection. The framework proposed here has theoretical significance for AI text identification and the naturalness of large models.

items.title: A Survey of Quality Evaluation on AI-Generated Lyrics
items.abstract: With the rapid development of generative artificial intelligence, AI lyric generation tools such as Suno, Baidu Wenxin Lyric Generator, and Doubao have been widely deployed. However, AI-generated lyrics commonly suffer from thematic deviation, emotional fragmentation, stylistic mismatch, grammatical inconsistency, and long-structure logical collapse, making objective quality evaluation a critical link for optimizing generation models and filtering outputs. This paper systematically reviews existing research on AI-generated lyric quality evaluation along three main lines: evaluation dimensions, datasets, and technical routes. Existing approaches are categorized into four technical routes: manual subjective evaluation, traditional statistical and rule-based modeling, deep learning and representation learning, and large language model and multimodal intelligent evaluation. A three-layer progressive evaluation indicator system is constructed, comprising the textual language layer, lyric-music layer, and artistic aesthetic layer. The findings reveal four key bottlenecks: the deep gap between automatic quantitative metrics and human subjective aesthetic experience, the modeling blind spot for Chinese phonological features and lyric-music coordination, the severe scarcity of dedicated annotated datasets with uneven cultural distribution, and the disconnect between static text quality evaluation and dynamic human-computer collaboration experience. Future research should advance in three directions: developing lyric-specific vertical large models integrating music theory, constructing audio-text cross-modal joint lyric-music evaluation systems, and building generation-evaluation-optimization closed-loop ecosystems for the entire creative workflow.

items.title: A systematic review of artificial intelligence driven energy management in smart grids
items.abstract: Abstract The rapid migration of electrical grids towards Smart Grid (SG) architectures produces high-dimensional data streams that must be processed intelligently in real time. Traditional modelling, optimisation, and control approaches cannot handle the growing complexity of contemporary power systems. This comprehensive study aims to provide a synopsis of AI applications in smart grid settings for load forecasting, transient and voltage stability analysis, fault detection, and cybersecurity. This work provides a unified analytical framework that links supervised, unsupervised, reinforcement, and ensemble learning techniques to specific smart grid operational problems, in contrast to prior surveys that address these areas separately. The main contributions are (i) a structured AI-smart grid functional taxonomy; (ii) critical analysis of the challenges of data quality, model interpretability, computational scalability and adversarial security; and (iii) a roadmap for explainable, reliable and carbon-neutral intelligent energy systems. Compared with more conventional methods, AI-based solutions often outperform them in prediction accuracy, stability, categorisation speed, and defect identification accuracy. However, there are major challenges in real-world deployment, standardisation and regulatory compliance.

items.title: A Systematic Review of Design Elements for Risk Communication in Hurricane Hazard Maps
items.abstract: Hurricanes are among the most destructive natural hazards. Effective risk communication through hurricane hazard maps is essential for reducing vulnerability to hazards. This paper examines how the public comprehends the design elements of risk category systems (colors, labels, and numbers of threat levels) in hazard maps through a systematic literature review and translates this evidence into recommendations for hurricane hazard map design. From an initial pool of 706 articles, 16 studies were selected for analysis. Key findings indicate that sequential color palettes such as yellow-to-red are preferred over rainbow schemes, that five to seven discrete risk classes support comprehension without overloading users, and that redundant encoding through labels and direct annotations improves accessibility for users with color vision deficiency. Findings provide insights for improving hurricane hazard map design and enhancing the communication of actionable hazard information.

items.title: Adaptive Artificial Intelligence Models for Enhancing Digital Inclusion and Sustainable Development in Underserved Communities
items.abstract: Technology is playing a vital role across various sectors like education, healthcare, agriculture, financial services, employment, governance, and social development. However, we still see significant digital inequalities, especially in underserved communities, particularly in rural and low-income areas. Here, challenges such as limited connectivity, high technology costs, lack of digital skills, language barriers, and inaccessible digital services hinder meaningful participation in the digital economy. This conceptual paper delves into how adaptive Artificial Intelligence (AI) models can boost digital inclusion and support sustainable development in these communities. It brings together insights from literature on artificial intelligence, digital inclusion, adaptive learning, responsible AI, and sustainable development. The paper introduces the Adaptive AI Digital Inclusion and Sustainable Development (AIDISD) framework, which is built around five key dimensions: accessibility, personalization, contextual adaptation, resource efficiency, and community empowerment. It explores potential applications in education, healthcare, agriculture, financial inclusion, employment, and public services. Additionally, the paper highlights challenges related to infrastructure, data scarcity, algorithmic bias, privacy, cybersecurity, affordability, digital literacy, and institutional capacity. The analysis emphasizes that adaptive AI should be viewed as part of a larger socio-technical strategy rather than just a standalone tech solution. For inclusive deployment, we need local participation, suitable infrastructure, responsible data governance, human oversight, and ongoing evaluation. Ultimately, the paper concludes that well-designed adaptive AI systems can foster more inclusive and sustainable digital ecosystems, provided they are affordable, locally relevant, accessible, transparent, and aligned with the Sustainable Development Goals.

items.title: Adaptive Curriculum Management: Reconstructing Higher Education Curriculum Governance in the Age of Artificial Intelligence
items.abstract: [English]: The rapid development of generative artificial intelligence challenges traditional higher education curriculum management models that rely on rigid 4-to-5-year review cycles. This article aims to reformulate curriculum governance to become more adaptive in the AI era. Through a systematic integrative review of studies on higher education curriculum governance and AI adaptation from 2024 to 2026, a pressing need to shift from static to dynamic structures was identified. To address this mismatch, the article proposes the Adaptive Higher Education Curriculum (AHEC) framework, which strategically divides curriculum components into stable macro-level foundations and rapidly renewable micro-level contents. The findings reveal that modern curriculum governance must leverage AI-based Continuous Curriculum Intelligence to monitor shifts in professional competencies and job market requirements in real time. Crucially, the framework enforces human-centered authority, ensuring that human educators retain ultimate responsibility for final decision-making. The article concludes that agile managerial governance and organic institutional self-renewal are essential keys to ensuring that higher education programs maintain long-term professional relevance in an AI-mediated society. [Indonesian]: Perkembangan pesat kecerdasan buatan (AI), terutama AI generatif, menantang model manajemen kurikulum tradisional di perguruan tinggi yang biasanya mengandalkan siklus peninjauan berkala setiap 4 hingga 5 tahun. Artikel ini bertujuan untuk merumuskan ulang tata kelola dan manajemen kurikulum agar menjadi lebih adaptif di era AI. Melalui metode analisis konseptual berbasis integrative systematic review terhadap studi tata kelola kurikulum perguruan tinggi dan adaptasi AI dari tahun 2024 hingga 2026, ditemukan adanya kebutuhan mendesak untuk bergeser dari struktur kurikulum statis ke dinamis. Artikel ini menawarkan kerangka kerja Adaptive Higher Education Curriculum (AHEC) yang membagi komponen kurikulum menjadi lapisan stabil dan lapisan yang dapat diperbarui secara cepat. Hasil kajian menunjukkan bahwa manajemen kurikulum masa depan harus memanfaatkan Continuous Curriculum Intelligence berbasis AI untuk memantau perubahan kompetensi kerja secara waktu-nyata, namun keputusan akhir dan penafsiran maknanya tetap berada di bawah kendali penuh dosen dan institusi. Kesimpulan dari artikel ini menegaskan bahwa ketangkasan tata kelola manajerial merupakan kunci utama agar kurikulum perguruan tinggi tetap relevan dengan kebutuhan zaman harus jelas, ringkas, dan deskriptif.

items.title: Adoption of generative artificial intelligence by university marketing students
items.abstract: The growing adoption of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) is transforming marketing education and increasing the need to understand the factors that drive its academic use among university students. This study aimed to analyze the determinants of GenAI adoption among university marketing students using the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology 2 (UTAUT2). A quantitative, explanatory, cross-sectional study was conducted with 310 marketing students from two Latin American universities in Peru and Costa Rica during the first academic semester of 2026. Participants were selected through non-probability purposive sampling. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire and analyzed through Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS version 4.1.1.8. The findings indicate that habit is the main determinant of both behavioral intention and actual use of GenAI tools, while hedonic motivation, facilitating conditions, and price value also show significant positive effects. Conversely, performance expectancy, effort expectancy, and social influence do not significantly influence behavioral intention. It is concluded that the adoption of GenAI among university marketing students is increasingly driven by habitual academic use rather than by traditional technology acceptance factors. These findings provide evidence to support institutional strategies for the responsible integration of GenAI into higher education.

items.title: Advances in clinical research on acute kidney injury, 2025–2026: A narrative review
items.abstract: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is a common clinical syndrome in the intensive care unit (ICU) that not only substantially increases in-hospital mortality but is also closely associated with the development and progression of chronic kidney disease, posing a serious threat to patient health. Recently, driven by advances in cutting-edge technologies such as liquid biopsy, multi-omics, and artificial intelligence, clinical research on AKI has achieved important breakthroughs. This narrative review systematically searched PubMed, Web of Science, EMBASE, and Cochrane Library databases for clinical studies published between January 2025 and August 2026, with particular emphasis on ICU-related AKI, especially surgery- and sepsis-associated AKI. The review focuses on three major aspects: early identification and risk stratification, optimization of prevention and treatment strategies, and individualized implementation and management of kidney replacement therapy. Between 2025 and 2026, clinical research on AKI yielded several important advances. These include the identification of multi-omics-based liquid-biopsy biomarkers and the development of causal deep-learning models enabling more accurate risk prediction. Terlipressin treatment improved reversal rates in selected patients with hepatorenal syndrome. However, multiple high-quality perioperative randomized controlled trials investigating blood pressure targets, artificial intelligence–assisted hemodynamic optimization, albumin infusion, and other interventions yielded negative or even harmful results, suggesting that hemodynamic interventions may have reached a benefit ceiling within current treatment paradigms. Meanwhile, the timing of kidney replacement therapy initiation, technical considerations, and weaning strategies have become increasingly customized. This review aims to provide the latest evidence-based information to guide clinical practice while identifying gaps in the current evidence and highlighting priorities for future research.

items.title: Advances in early human embryonic development and organogenesis from spatiotemporal multi-omics
items.abstract: Deciphering early human embryonic development and organogenesis is constrained by limited access to in vivo specimens and the intrinsic complexity of spatiotemporal cell fate dynamics. Recent advances in spatiotemporal multi-omics have begun to overcome these barriers by enabling the reconstruction of in silico human embryos and developmental trajectories with spatial and temporal resolution. These approaches have revealed fundamental principles of lineage specification, cell migration, tissue morphogenesis, and axial patterning in early human development. In this Review, we summarize how single-cell and spatial multi-omics technologies, particularly spatial transcriptomics, have transformed the study of human early embryogenesis, organogenesis, and stem-cell-derived embryoid systems. We highlight analytical frameworks that integrate spatial context, temporal progression, and multimodal datasets, and discuss how biological discovery and algorithmic innovation have co-evolved. Finally, we outline how artificial intelligence, foundation models, and large-scale multimodal learning may eventually enable predictive and causal modeling of human development, while addressing current technical, interpretability, and ethical challenges.

items.title: Advancing Clinical Genomic Analysis with a Skill-Centred Agent
items.abstract: Clinical genomic analysis requires experts to integrate evolving guidelines, databases, and computational evidence. As sequencing has become increasingly accessible, this complex and labor-intensive process has become a major bottleneck to the timely use of genomic information in clinical decision-making. To fill this gap, we developed ClinGeX, a large-language-model agent that composes 105 curated executable skills through task-specific retrieval and dependency-aware orchestration. On 223 temporally held-out benchmark cases, ClinGeX achieved 71.7\% macro-averaged task-level concordance with expert reference classifications, compared with 45.7\% for the strongest comparator. In a three-condition, counterbalanced human-AI collaboration study, 45 clinical genomic professionals assessed 135 clinically derived cases under routine (no AI assistance), DeepSeek-assisted and ClinGeX-assisted conditions. ClinGeX assistance increased raw case-level concordance across criterion-level variant analysis, genomic interpretation in rare disease and molecular oncology decision-making (51.1\%, 57.8\%, 64.4\% versus 15.6\%, 31.1\%, 20.0\% in comparator conditions) and reduced reported interpretation time in all scenarios. During an exploratory one-month real-world non-interventional assessment, 11 experienced professionals submitted feedback on 96 self-selected analysis episodes and reported frequent conclusion adoption and time savings. These findings support executable domain skills as a promising approach to augment specialist genomic interpretation.

items.title: Advancing morphological profiling with self-supervised learning through comparative insights into representation learning of cellular perturbations
items.abstract: Abstract Self-supervised learning (SSL) enables scalable, label-free foundation models (FMs) that learn task-agnostic representations directly from images, bypassing cell segmentation and feature engineering inherent to classical morphological profiling. We present a large-scale evaluation of SSL FMs for image-based phenotypic profiling, covering contrastive (DINO), masked-based generative (MAE, iTPN) and hybrid (DINOv2) learning mechanisms, pretrained on all unannotated chemical perturbations from the Joint Undertaking for Morphological Profiling–Cell Painting (JUMP–CP) dataset (119,876 compounds, ~1.77 million images, 7 laboratories). Here we show that top-performing SSL models outperformed CellProfiler in compound-replicate retrieval on the held-out JUMP–Target2 set (302 annotated compounds, P ≤ 0.001). DINO and DINOv2 generalized across diverse perturbations and cell types, outperforming CellProfiler with 31–37% gains in site-averaged mean average precision for mechanism-of-action retrieval on EU-OPENSCREEN Bioactives (2,464 compounds), and consistently surpassing masked-based models across all benchmarks. This study provides a systematic assessment of SSL approaches for advancing morphological profiling and offers pretrained FMs to accelerate drug discovery.

items.title: Adversarial Pilot Injection Against AI-Based CSI Feedback in FDD Massive MIMO Systems
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI)-based channel state information (CSI) feedback reduces overhead in frequency division duplexing (FDD) massive multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems, yet its reconstructed CSI depends on the integrity of pilot acquisition. This paper identifies and evaluates the attack path of adversarial pilot injection against this feedback. A transmitted disturbance can damage the user-side estimation before encoding; correctly delivered quantized bits can still represent a contaminated channel estimate. We model this path through attacker propagation, linear minimum mean square error estimation, compression, quantization, and decoding under a total transmit-energy constraint. An adversarial perturbation generator (APG) implements the attack using channel statistics without current legitimate CSI or instantaneous attacker-channel observations at deployment. At a Rician attacker-channel factor of 10~dB and a transmit perturbation-to-signal ratio of $-4$~dB, APG produces a normalized mean-square error (NMSE) of 0.84~dB in base-station CSI reconstruction, compared with $-10.31$~dB for Gaussian interference. Estimator-targeted and reconstruction-targeted attacks yield different error orderings, and reconstruction damage also degrades beamforming. As a countermeasure, alternating adversarial training (AAT) adapts the feedback encoder and decoder to contaminated pilots. With condition-matched training and APGs reoptimized for the final receiver, AAT reduces NMSE by 2.40--3.79~dB across six representative channel--power conditions. The results demonstrate the importance of protecting pilot acquisition alongside quantized feedback delivery.
